clue.text: Playschool subject? It's an outrage!

definitions.meaning: Sheridan's comedy The School for ... names its subject in the title, so the play's school is for this
a disgraceful affair that causes public outrage

explanation.surface: A children's television topic turns out to be shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playschool' suggests the BBC children's programme; read it as play + school, Sheridan's The School for Scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a disgraceful event that provokes public outrage, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Girl entertained by hares and rabbits

indicators.note: the girl is held as a guest inside the words hares and rabbits, so her letters run across them

explanation.surface: A young woman is amused by the antics of hares and rabbits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a girl's first name, so the generic word stands for an example.

clue.text: Merchant ship from Greek city coming to journey's end

parts.note: Argos is an ancient city in the Peloponnese

indicators.note: the end of the word journey's is its last letter

explanation.surface: A trading vessel sails from a Greek port to finish its voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large merchant ship, originally one from Ragusa, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: The wife and kids I left in farm buildings

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter I goes from the kids

parts.note: bairns is Scottish and northern English for children
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man abandons his wife and children among the barns of a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' for wife comes from Cockney 'my old Dutch' (short for duchess); BAIRNS less I gives BARNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch barns are open-sided farm structures with curved roofs used for storing hay.

clue.text: Explorer's last seen on sledge with a pistol

indicators.note: in a down clue the explorer's letter sits on, after, the sledge

parts.note: a luge is a small racing toboggan

indicators.note: the last letter of the word Explorer's is wanted

explanation.surface: A polar explorer is last spotted on a sledge, armed with a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luger is a German semi-automatic handgun, a proprietary name for one kind of pistol.

clue.text: Gemstone returned to dreadful party leader

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole run of to, dreadful and the leader is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
dire means dreadful

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter of party

explanation.surface: A precious stone is handed back to an awful political boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the whole string TODIREP (TO, DIRE, P) backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gem variety of olivine, an example of a gemstone.

clue.text: Mobile phone with more influential output?

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters of phone and more are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mobile phone with more clout than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' reads as one object; 'Mobile' is the anagram signal on PHONE and MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheromone is a chemical an animal secretes to influence others' behaviour, so a whimsical description.

clue.text: Rotten Row

definitions.meaning: a line of people or things side by side

explanation.surface: Rotten Row is the bridle path in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a riding track in Hyde Park, London; split it into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means rotten or foul, and as a noun a row or line.

clue.text: Work in the garden for Dr Arnold, say?

definitions.meaning: to remove spent flowers from a plant
Thomas Arnold, Victorian headmaster of Rugby School, is a head who has died

explanation.surface: A gardening task fit for a famous Victorian headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Thomas Arnold was the celebrated headmaster of Rugby School who died in 1842: a dead head.
explanation.definitionFit: To deadhead is to snip off faded blooms, a gardening verb; the second sense is a punning description.

clue.text: Old maids in the capital of Texas given American sausages

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, here of Texas

parts.note: weenies is a US word for frankfurters

explanation.surface: Elderly spinsters in Austin are served hot dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Texas' tempts towards Austin, but it is the initial T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweenies were historically between-maids, servants helping both cook and housemaid, so old-fashioned maids.

clue.text: It's dark almost on time

indicators.note: in an across clue on means following, so time comes after

parts.note: nigh means nearly

explanation.surface: Evening falls, and it is very nearly time.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness, as in 'after dark', so the noun matches.

clue.text: Fruit grower's first to hire again

indicators.note: the first letter of the word grower's is taken

parts.note: re-engage means take on again as an employee

explanation.surface: A fruit grower's priority is taking staff back on.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of sweet green plum, an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Plant seen before school break

indicators.note: the break is put in front of the school

parts.note: a rest is a break from activity
Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A plant is noticed just before the school holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a well-known English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Restharrow is a tough-rooted wild plant of the pea family, once said to halt harrows.

clue.text: Steer clear of military command

definitions.meaning: short form of 'attention', barked on the parade ground

explanation.surface: Avoid the army's orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun is to avoid; ''shun' is also the clipped drill order for attention.

clue.text: Cars crashed with golden slumber caused by this?

indicators.note: cars that crash are smashed up, so the letters of Cars and golden are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wrecked cars and golden sleep somehow linked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden Slumbers' is an old lullaby (and a Beatles song); the definition describes what a lullaby brings on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradlesong is a lullaby sung to send a baby to sleep, so it brings on slumber.

clue.text: Apt to take what belongs to others

definitions.text: to take what belongs to others
definitions.meaning: to seize for oneself without permission

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to help themselves to other people's things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apt to' reads as 'inclined to'; split after 'Apt' for two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropriate as an adjective means fitting, and as a verb to take something for one's own use.

clue.text: Job given to jokers with received views?

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
cards are jokers in the sense of comical people

explanation.surface: A job is handed to some comedians with conventional opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received views' suggests orthodox opinions; here it is pictures of places that arrive in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture postcards show views and are received through the mail, a playful description.

clue.text: Old boy rolling India's rock

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: rolling means tumbling about, so the letters of India's are mixed up

parts.note: the letters INDIAS, the S included

explanation.surface: A former pupil tours India's rocky terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark volcanic glass, an example of a rock.

clue.text: Having swallowed half of loaf, bolt a piece of meat

indicators.note: the bolting word takes the half-loaf inside it

parts.note: to bolt is to escape, run away

indicators.note: the first half of the word loaf is taken

explanation.surface: Wolfing half a loaf, someone gulps down a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like gobbling food, but it means run away; 'Having swallowed' puts the half-loaf inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, such as veal, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Liquidation for functional part?

definitions.meaning: the winding up of a company is the end of a business
the working end of a tool or weapon

explanation.surface: Is winding up a company its most useful feature?
explanation.definitionFit: The business end is the working part of a tool; read literally it is a firm's closure.

clue.text: Draw sailor's head on boat

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of sailor's

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Sketch the seaman's head as he stands aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To sketch is to draw roughly, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Professionals have it on toast

parts.note: pros is short for professionals
taken as written

explanation.surface: The experts are eating it spread on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on toast' looks like breakfast; 'toast' is a drinking salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin drinking toast meaning 'may it benefit'.

clue.text: Country and western finale by Gershwin

indicators.note: by means next to, so the finale follows Gershwin

parts.note: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

indicators.note: a finale is the ending, so the last letter of western

explanation.surface: A country and western finale written by Gershwin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country and western' reads as a music genre; 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in south-west Asia, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Vessel for taking away Naval Reserve?

definitions.text: Vessel for taking away Naval Reserve?

parts.words: Vessel for taking away Naval Reserve?
parts.note: reserve is reticence, ice in breaking the ice; also a ship that clears frozen sea

explanation.surface: A ship designed to remove a naval reserve force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naval Reserve' suggests a military force; reserve also means reticence, the ice that a friendly opener breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: This ship smashes through frozen seas, and an opening remark dispels social reserve, which is a punning reading.

clue.text: Fish for lutenist

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of the carp family
Julian ... was a celebrated English guitarist and lute player

explanation.surface: A fish served for a lute player.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a freshwater fish, and Julian Bream a famous English lutenist.

clue.text: Indian food served in second half

indicators.note: the food is dished up within the words second half

explanation.surface: Indian food arrives at half-time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal is an Indian dish of spiced lentils or split pulses.

clue.text: Engine assembled for son or heir

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters of son or heir are built into a new order

explanation.surface: An engine is built for a son or an heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron horse' is an old nickname for a steam locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is a dated nickname for a railway locomotive, a kind of engine.

clue.text: Food divided by English conspirator

indicators.note: the food is split by the English letter placed inside it

parts.note: oats are grain used as food

explanation.surface: Food is shared out by an Englishman who plotted.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates fabricated the Popish Plot of 1678, an anti-Catholic conspiracy story.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates was the English plotter behind the invented Popish Plot.

clue.text: Bugs almost expendable

indicators.note: almost means nearly, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: needless means unnecessary, able to be done without

explanation.surface: Insects are nearly dispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' looks like insects; it is the verb meaning annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs and needles are both verbs for annoying or irritating someone.

clue.text: Picture beakers just filled from the tea urn?

parts.note: mugs are drinking cups, beakers

parts.words: just filled from the tea urn?
parts.note: freshly poured tea is hot

explanation.surface: A picture of cups freshly poured from the urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is a police photograph of a face, a kind of picture.
